cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where user-supplied URLs or redirect targets are used in server-side network operations (redirects, HTTP requests, OS commands, DNS) without proper validation, allowing attackers to redirect users to malicious sites, perform SSRF, leak credentials, or execute commands.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled filenames, archive entries, path fragments, or resource names into file read, write, delete, extraction, or resource-loading APIs. Report code paths where the normalized absolute path is not checked to remain under the intended base directory before the file operation. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should normalize and canonicalize the resolved path, then enforce a base-directory prefix or equivalent containment check.

mechanism.missing_guard: the normalized absolute path is not checked to remain under the intended base directory before the file operation
mechanism.name: path traversal through missing canonical prefix check
mechanism.sink_shape: file read, write, delete, extraction, or resource-loading APIs
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled filenames, archive entries, path fragments, or resource names
mechanism.typical_fix: normalize and canonicalize the resolved path, then enforce a base-directory prefix or equivalent containment check

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use absolute path to executable, reject non-http URL prefixes, or use safe API (java.awt.Desktop).
sub_patterns.name: OS command injection via unsanitized URL in system command
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-supplied URL is concatenated into an OS command string without sanitization, allowing injection of shell metacharacters.
